Without Noctalia it exits 4 (on Plasma use System Settings > Power Management). Noctalia has no screensaver, so there is no screensaver toggle; notify dnd|snooze already cover reminders. bxrig dns [cloudflare|google|quad9|dhcp|custom IP[,IP...]] lists or sets the DNS servers of the active NetworkManager connections (loopback, bridge, tunnel and container devices are skipped) with nmcli connection modify NAME ipv4.dns ... ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes ipv6.dns ... ipv6.ignore-auto-dns yes , then connection up NAME . dhcp clears them. A plan (exit 2) without --yes ; a bad IP exits 2. bxrig kernel list|install NAME|remove NAME . list shows the running kernel, the installed kernel packages and the linux-cachyos* kernels you could add (nvidia, zfs, rc and headers packages are left out). install is sudo pacman -S --needed NAME NAME-headers (the name must match linux(-[a-z0-9]+)* and exist in the repos, else exit 4 or 2). remove refuses the running kernel (judged from uname -r and the package suffix) and the last installed kernel (exit 4). It never edits the bootloader and never picks the default: the boot entries come from the kernel packages' hooks and you choose in the boot menu. bxrig security status|fingerprint|fido2|ssh-server|passwordless-sudo . Guards: only /etc/pam.d/sudo is ever changed (never login, SDDM or the lock screen); the line is auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so or auth sufficient pam_u2f.so cue inserted before the first auth line and marked with a # bxrig KIND comment, so your password still works without the reader or key; a file with no auth line is left alone (exit 4); the original is kept once as /etc/pam.d/sudo.bxrig-backup ; off removes exactly the marked line; running on twice adds one line. fingerprint enroll runs fprintd-enroll ; fido2 register runs pamu2fcfg into ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys , and fido2 on refuses (exit 4) until that file exists. passwordless-sudo on writes /etc/sudoers.d/50-bxrig-nopasswd ( USER ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL , user from $USER` and checked against `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$ ) only after visudo -cf passes, with mode 440; off removes it. ssh-server on|off installs openssh and runs systemctl enable|disable --now sshd.service . Everything is a plan (exit 2) without --yes , and --dry-run prints the exact line or file. Agents: the Agent menu runs ai launch NAME ; there is no separate agent command. Menu: Trigger > Toggle (stay awake), Setup > DNS, Security, Time, Kernel. Verified: tests/tweaks-test.sh and tests/security-test.sh (fake nmcli, pacman, noctalia, uname, visudo, sudo and fake /etc/pam.d and /etc/sudoers.d ). Not verified on a real machine: PAM behavior with a real reader or key, nmcli on your connection names, kernel removal. 13.40 The command reference and bxrig help (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) One source: docs/reference/cli.json holds, for every command, its group, a one-sentence summary, its usage lines, examples, whether it needs --yes ( mutates ) and an optional note. bootstrap/gen-docs.sh writes docs/reference/commands.md (the docs page: flags, exit codes, the JSON envelope, an index by group, then every command with usage and examples) and src/bxrig/HelpData.bx (the same data inside the binary). bxrig help (and bare bxrig ) lists every command by group with its summary; bxrig help NAME prints the summary, usage, whether --yes is needed, examples and notes; --json returns the same data; an unknown name exits 2. Drift checks: gen-docs.sh --check fails when a command in src/Main.bx has no entry, an entry has no command, a usage line does not start with its command, an example names no real command, a summary does not end in a full stop, or the text contains an em dash. The usage lines of older commands are copied from the usage text in src/Main.bx ; the newer classes ( appearance , display , power , time , toggle , dns , kernel , security ) print their own usage, so their entries are written by hand and must be updated with the class. Verified: tests/help-test.sh (the groups, a command, JSON, unknown, and that the generated files are current). 13.41 NAS as a first-class namespace (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxrig nas keeps every NAS you use in ~/.config/bxrig/nas.json (name, host, protocol smb or nfs , user, optional SMB version, and the shares you mounted). discover browses the network with avahi-browse -rtp _smb._tcp and _nfs._tcp (IPv4 only). setup installs cifs-utils nfs-utils smbclient avahi nss-mdns rsync and enables avahi-daemon (a plan without --yes ; every tool was checked in the Arch repos and its binary exists after install). add NAME --host=H needs --user and a password for SMB ( --ask-password , typed hidden, or --password-file=F ); the password goes to the keyring as BXRIG_NAS_<NAME>_PASSWORD and never into nas.json . NFS needs neither. Names are ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$ . shares NAME lists SMB shares with smbclient -g -L HOST -A AUTHFILE (the auth file is a private temp file, deleted after; no password on a command line; IPC$ and other hidden shares are dropped) or NFS exports with showmount -e --no-headers . mount|unmount NAME SHARE mounts at ~/NAS/NAME/LEAF ( BXRIG_NAS_HOME overrides) with sudo mount -t cifs|nfs ; the SMB options are credentials=/etc/bxrig/nas/NAME.cred,uid,gid,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0600,dir_mode=0700 plus vers= only when you set one (otherwise the kernel negotiates the highest version both sides support). The credentials file is root-only (mode 600) because mount.cifs reads it as root ; the plan says so. auto on|off NAME SHARE writes <escaped-path>.mount and .automount units to /etc/systemd/system ( Options=...,nofail , TimeoutSec=20 , TimeoutIdleSec=600 , wanted by multi-user.target ), runs daemon-reload and enable --now , so a sleeping NAS never blocks login. off disables and removes them; a NAS with automatic mounts is not removed (exit 4) until they are off. test NAME [SHARE] checks: reachable (TCP 445 or 2049), signed in or exports readable, mounted ( findmnt ), writable (a probe file), free space. Exit 4 when a check fails. sync NAME SRC --to=SHARE[/PATH] is a plain rsync -a mirror to a mounted share. Nothing is deleted from the NAS unless you add --delete , and the plan says so in capitals. use NAME SHARE [--path=bxrig-backup] records targets.nas-NAME in ~/.config/bxrig/backup.json ( {type: nas, nas, share, path} ); backup data setup reads it. Verified: tests/nas-test.sh with fake avahi-browse, smbclient, showmount, findmnt, rsync, sudo and a fake /etc . Not verified on a real Synology: DSM share permissions, SMB signing, NFS export options, nss-mdns name resolution. 13.42 refresh and reinstall (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) No factory reset. bxrig refresh COMPONENT puts managed config back to what BxRig ships and never installs a package. Components: hyprland (runs keys apply , appearance apply , display apply ; with --starter also the starter hyprland.lua ), noctalia ( theme set CURRENT , appearance apply , noctalia msg config-reload ; with --starter also the Noctalia starter files), terminals (the starter config of each installed terminal, then the theme includes), shell ( starship.toml , the shell init and the line in .zshrc or .bashrc ), nvim ( editor refresh ), theme ( theme set CURRENT , appearance apply ), all , and list . Semantics are the config service's: a clean file is left alone, a missing or outdated one is written, a file you edited ( drifted ) is kept and reported, and --force overwrites it after a backup ( config history , config restore ). A link or special file in the way blocks (exit 8 in the service, shown as blocked). Without --yes it prints the plan and exits 2; --dry-run exits 0. reinstall is init --rerun : the way to install packages again. Verified: tests/refresh-test.sh (temp home, fake bxrig that logs the commands, a fake terminal): plan and dry run write nothing, files are written, a second run rewrites nothing clean, edits are kept, --force overwrites and takes a backup, each component runs its commands. 13.43 Backups: the config layer (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Three layers, one command. bxrig backup config (your BxRig setup), backup snapshots (the system, Btrfs with snapper) and backup data (your files, restic) are built in that order; backup send and backup export move any of them, and timemachine shows them all. This section is the config layer; the others are added below as they land. A snapshot is ~/.local/share/bxrig/backups/config/ID.tar.gz (mode 600) plus ID.json . ID is yyyyMMddTHHmmss (with -xxxx when two land in the same second). Inside: files/ (paths under your home), packages.txt ( pacman -Qqe ), foreign.txt ( pacman -Qqm ), meta.json , and secrets.bxs only with --with-secrets (the output of bxrig secrets export , encrypted with a passphrase you type). What is tracked (under your home): .config/bxrig , hypr , noctalia , ghostty , kitty , foot , alacritty , starship.toml , nvim , btop , fish , git , mimeapps.list , xdg-terminals.list , .zshrc , .bashrc , .gitconfig , .ssh/config . backup config add|remove PATH changes the list (stored in backup.json ); SSH keys, gnupg , .. and absolute paths are refused. .git , node_modules and *.log are skipped. Restore shows a plan (which files are created or replaced; exit 2 without --yes ), takes a safety snapshot of the present first, then copies the files back ( --only=PATH limits it). --packages installs the explicit packages that are missing and exist in the repositories with sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm ; AUR and local ones are listed for yay , never installed from here. diff ID compares a snapshot with now (files same, changed, missing, and missing packages). Automatic: auto is on by default. Before update apply , system update , init , reinstall and refresh (with --yes , never --dry-run ) a snapshot is taken quietly, with the reason before <command> ; it never stops the command. The newest 30 are kept ( prune --keep=N ). Verified: tests/backup-config-test.sh (temp home, fake pacman, sudo and bxrig). Not verified: a restore on a different machine. backup snapshots (system snapshots). Btrfs root: snapper. setup [--home] installs snapper snap-pac (and grub-btrfs only when GRUB is in use), creates the root config ( snapper -c root create-config / ; --home adds /home ), sets the timeline to 5 hourly, 7 daily, 2 weekly, 1 monthly, 0 yearly ( snapper set-config TIMELINE_* ), and enables snapper-timeline.timer and snapper-cleanup.timer (and grub-btrfsd.service ). snap-pac takes a snapshot before and after every pacman transaction through its own hooks. Other filesystems: it installs Timeshift (rsync mode), which takes full copies and needs one visit to its window to pick a disk. list reads snapper --jsonout -c CONFIG list (snapshot 0, the live system, is left out); create [--description=T] is snapper create --description T -p ; delete ID ; changes ID is snapper status ID..0 ; restore ID PATH is snapper undochange ID..0 PATH (files changed since are replaced, files that did not exist then are removed, so the plan says so). There is no automatic whole-system rollback : rolling back a Btrfs root depends on your subvolume layout, so you boot the snapshot from the GRUB menu and follow the Arch wiki, or restore folders with restore . Everything that changes the system is a plan without --yes . Not verified on real Btrfs: the JSON shape of snapper --jsonout list (the parser accepts a bare array or an object holding one array), the timers, undochange . Tested with fakes in tests/backup-snapshots-test.sh . backup data (your files, restic). A target is a place a restic repository lives: local (a path), nas (made by nas use , at ~/NAS/NAME/SHARE/PATH ), sftp ( sftp:user@host:/path ; port as sftp:-p N user@host:/path ), rest ( rest:URL ), s3 ( s3:ENDPOINT/BUCKET/PATH , AWS when no endpoint; works for DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, MinIO), b2 ( b2:BUCKET:PATH ), azure ( azure:CONTAINER:/PATH ), gs ( gs:BUCKET:/PATH , with GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS as the project and the service-account file) and rclone ( rclone:REMOTE:PATH ; FTP and any rclone service). The environment variable names ( AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID , AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY , AWS_DEFAULT_REGION , B2_ACCOUNT_ID , B2_ACCOUNT_KEY , AZURE_ACCOUNT_NAME , AZURE_ACCOUNT_KEY , RESTIC_REST_USERNAME , RESTIC_REST_PASSWORD ) and the address forms were read from restic's own documentation; the flags used ( -r via RESTIC_REPOSITORY , backup --tag --exclude --exclude-caches --one-file-system , forget --keep-daily|weekly|monthly --prune , snapshots --json , ls --json , restore --target --include , check --read-data-subset ) from the installed restic 0.19.1. Keys go straight to the keyring ( target add ... --ask-keys , typed hidden, or --keys-file with KEY=VALUE lines) as BXRIG_BACKUP_<TARGET>_<KEY> ; the repository password is generated at init (24 random bytes, hex) and kept as BXRIG_BACKUP_<TARGET>_PASSWORD , with a reminder that losing it loses the backups. restic is started with these in its environment , never on a command line, and no key is written to backup.json . run backs up the include list (default Projects code dev Documents .ssh , only the ones that exist) skipping the exclude list (default node_modules target .gradle __pycache__ .venv venv .cache .next *.tmp ) and cache folders, on one filesystem, tagged bxrig ; list , files , restore ID --to=DIR [--include=PATH] (into a folder you name, never over your files by itself), verify [--deep] ( restic check , --read-data-subset 5% ), forget (retention 7 daily, 4 weekly, 6 monthly by default, retention changes it; deletes older backups for good, so it is a plan first), schedule hourly|daily|off (user units bxrig-backup.service and .timer : ConditionACPower=true so it skips on battery, Persistent=true to catch up, a random delay up to 15 minutes; a failed scheduled run sends a Noctalia or notify-send notification). An unmounted NAS share exits 4 with the nas mount command. Verified: tests/backup-data-test.sh with a fake restic that records its arguments and the variables it was given. Not verified against a real cloud account, NAS or restic repository in this environment. backup send and backup export (moving backups). send ID|all --to=TARGET [--from=TARGET] is restic copy into a second repository (a NAS and a cloud bucket, for a 3-2-1 setup): the destination is RESTIC_REPOSITORY , the source goes in RESTIC_FROM_REPOSITORY with RESTIC_FROM_PASSWORD_COMMAND=printenv BXRIG_FROM_PW , so no password is on a command line. restic reads one set of AWS_* , B2_* ... variables, so two repositories that need different values for the same variable (two S3 accounts) are refused (exit 4) with a pointer to rclone sync . export data ID --to=FILE is restic dump --archive tar|zip --target FILE ID PATH (zip when the name ends in .zip ; --path limits it to a folder; an existing file is never overwritten), export config ID --to=FILE.tar.gz copies a config snapshot out as one file. Config snapshots travel with the data backups : ~/.local/share/bxrig/backups/config is in the default include list, so a NAS or cloud target protects them with no extra step. System snapshots are not exportable. Tested in tests/backup-move-test.sh with a fake restic. 13.44 BxTimeMachine, the backup screen (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxrig timemachine [--demo] [--local] (also bxrig bxtimemachine ) is BxTimeMachine , a full-screen terminal UI on MatchBox's canvas (the same one as the wizard) over bxrig backup timeline [--json] [--local] , which lists every backup in one structure: rows system (snapper), config (config snapshots), files-NAME (one per data target, from restic snapshots --json ) and mirror-NAME (recorded nas sync runs). A point is { id, time, epoch, label, tier, size } ; tier is by age (hourly up to a day, daily to a week, weekly to 5 weeks, monthly to a year, yearly after). A target that fails is a row with an error (unreachable, not initialized, NAS not mounted), never a failure of the whole timeline; --local leaves out the targets that need the network so the screen opens at once. BXRIG_TIMELINE_FILE injects a timeline (tests); BXRIG_NOW_EPOCH fixes the clock. The screen: places as rows over a time axis (newest on the right; zoom 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year, all; the axis grows to keep the chosen backup in view), points coloured by tier, a guide line through the chosen moment, the chosen backup as a card with the older ones stacked behind it, counts by tier for the place, and the brand gradient with Powered by BoxLang. Keys: left and right (or h l) through time, up and down (k j) between places, plus and minus zoom, enter open, d diff, r restore, e export, s send, n back up now, / filter in the browser, ? help, q or esc leave; the mouse picks a point, a place or a zoom chip and the wheel moves through time. Under 90 by 30 cells it asks for a bigger window. What it runs: it only runs bxrig commands, and every change goes through a plan first : it runs the command with --dry-run , shows the plan, and runs it with --yes only on y . Open: backup data files ID --json , backup config show ID --json or backup snapshots changes N . Restore: backup data restore ID --to=~/Restored/ID [--include=PATH] , backup config restore ID [--only=PATH] or backup snapshots restore N PATH (a folder must be picked first). Export: backup export data|config . Send: backup send ID --from=PLACE --to=PLACE (file backups only; a destination picker). Back up now: backup data run , backup config now or backup snapshots create . Config snapshots reach a NAS or the cloud through the data backups (they are in its include list). --demo shows a made-up timeline (every kind of place and every tier) and runs nothing: plans and results say what the command would have been. tools/record-timemachine.py records the demo in a pseudo-terminal (pyte, Pillow, ffmpeg) into named screenshots and a video. Verified: tests/time_machine_test.bxs (the model, the keys and intents, the date maths, and what each screen shows via render_to_string ) and tests/timeline-test.sh . Not yet tried: against real restic repositories, a real NAS or snapper on Btrfs; with a real terminal beyond the recorded demo. 13.45 The backup pages of the wizard (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) The wizard has three pages after Containers, in this order: NAS ( nas_use , nas_name , nas_host , nas_protocol , nas_user , nas_share , nas_auto ), Remote backups ( remote_type none, s3, b2, azure, gs, sftp, rclone or local, with remote_name , remote_endpoint , remote_bucket , remote_region , remote_container , remote_project , remote_credentials , remote_host , remote_user , remote_remote , remote_path ) and Backups ( backup_layers : config, snapshots, data; backup_schedule : daily, hourly, off). The old tools-only backups question is gone; restic is installed when files are protected. No secret is in an answer. The plan steps are commands that ask for them in the terminal while the setup runs: nas add ... --ask-password (SMB) and backup data target add ... --ask-keys (S3, B2, Azure). Every NAS, target and schedule step is optional, so a missing network or a wrong password never stops the rest of the plan. Steps in order: nas-setup , nas-add , nas-mount , nas-auto , nas-use ; backup-remote ; per place backup-init-PLACE , backup-default , backup-schedule ; backup-snapshots ; backup-config-off when the config layer is not chosen. backup data run --all (used by the schedule) backs up every place that is set up; backup data default NAME chooses the place used without --target . Verified: tests/init_plan_test.bxs (the steps for a Synology over SMB, NFS, S3, Google, a disk, a missing address) and the wizard tests (13 pages in Basic mode). 13.46 The TUI kit and the Control Center (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Kit ( TuiKit , TuiList , TuiRunner ): every terminal screen paints with one kit (palette, text, gradient, panels, click regions, tabs, scrolling list, modal and plan box, toast, key bar, meter, badge, sparkline), keeps list state in TuiList (cursor, scroll, filter) and runs through TuiRunner (one loop that always restores the terminal). The wizard and BxTimeMachine use it; their tests did not change. Command: tui [PAGE] [--demo] [--json] . Without --json it needs a terminal (exit 4 without one). --json prints the page's data ( { data, attention, cursor } ) and exits 0; an unknown page or more than one word exits 2. --demo uses made-up data and runs nothing. Page interface: a class with id() title() load() keys() paint( kit, x, y, w, h, tick, phase ) onKey( key ) act( hit ) onScroll( dir ) . A key, click or scroll returns an intent: {} , { action: "goto", page } , { action: "launch", target } (leave and run that screen, then come back to the same page) or { action: "cli", title, args } . A cli intent first runs the command with --dry-run and shows the output as the plan; only y runs it with --yes , and the result box follows. Keys: Tab and Shift+Tab (or ] and [ ) change page, Left moves to the sidebar, Right or Enter returns, q, Escape and Ctrl+c leave. Dashboard (built): needs attention (updates from checkupdates when installed, backups older than 2 days or none, disk 85% or more, battery 20% or less and not charging), system meters ( /proc , df , /sys/class/power_supply , BXRIG_POWER_DIR ), machines ( db list --json and vm list --json ) and backups (the timeline, --local ). Every part is read alone; a part that fails is left out. BXRIG_DASHBOARD_FILE (a JSON file) replaces the machine for tests. Table pages ( ListPage with a provider: id title columns load( query ) actions detail style hint live emptyText ): BoxLang ( bvm list , bvm current , read leniently: every version number on a line, a * or (current) marks the active one; unverified against a working bvm), Java ( bxrig java list ), Versions (BoxLang, MatchBox, Java, Node; Enter opens the deep page), Ports ( ss -ltnpH and ps ; one row per port and pid; two owners on a port is a conflict), Packages (live pkg search ), Shortcuts ( keys show ), Machines (VMs only: vm list ), Databases ( db list ), Storage ( nas list , cloud status ), Secrets ( secrets list , a value only through secrets get --show ), Themes ( theme list ) and Logs ( journalctl -b -o json -p , priority cycles error, warning, info). Keys compare exactly ( K is not k ). While a page takes text (a filter or a search) it gets every key, including q and Escape. More intents: { action: "exec", title, argv, plan } (a plan you wrote, then the program), { action: "show", title, args } (run bxrig ARGS at once and show the output; only for reads), { action: "ask", title, prompt, make } (a text box; make( value ) returns the next intent) and { action: "reload" } . Icons (2026-11-14): TuiKit.icon( name ) returns a Nerd Font glyph (Font Awesome range, plus e738 for Java; all checked against the Symbols Nerd Font) or "" when icons are off. Pages say which icon they use with icon() . tui --icons=on|off and BXRIG_ICONS decide; otherwise a Nerd Font found by fc-list turns them on. No emoji: their width differs between terminals and breaks the cell layout. Not built yet: BxTimeMachine inside the sidebar (it opens full screen and returns), mise and nvm actions, rebinding with a key-capture. Known MatchBox quirk: reading a missing key of a parsed JSON struct inside a try block in a nested function panicked the native runner while the interpreter did not; the code checks the key first. To be reproduced and reported upstream. 13.47 Java, Maven and Gradle (decided with the owner 2026-11-14) bxrig java ( Java.bx ): list|available|install MAJOR|default ID|MAJOR [--unset]|remove ID|env [ID] . Homes: ~/.local/share/bxrig/java/ID (BxRig's own Temurin installs from the Adoptium API: /v3/info/available_releases and /v3/binary/latest/MAJOR/ga/linux/x64/jdk/hotspot/normal/eclipse , both checked), SDKMAN ( ~/.sdkman/candidates/java ) and /usr/lib/jvm . Only BxRig's own installs are removed. The default is java.sh and java.fish in ~/.config/bxrig , sourced by the three shell starters. Install and default and remove plan first (exit 2 without --yes ). Overrides for tests: BXRIG_JAVA_DIR , BXRIG_JAVA_SYSTEM_DIR , BXRIG_SDKMAN_DIR , BXRIG_ADOPTIUM_API , BXRIG_JAVA_DOWNLOAD_URL . bxrig sdk ( Sdk.bx , decided 2026-11-14: SDKMAN is the way to install Java, Maven and Gradle): status|setup|list C|available C|install C V|default C V|remove C V , C is java, maven or gradle. A development inbox: Mailpit ( axllent/mailpit ) in a container named bxrig-mail , SMTP on 127.0.0.1:1025 , web inbox and REST API on 127.0.0.1:8025 (both ports can be changed; ports are 1024 to 65535 and must differ, else exit 4). Everything is bound to 127.0.0.1 . The engine is the one db engine chose (podman by default). Thrown away on stop. Without --keep the container runs with --rm and no volume, so stop deletes it and its mail. With --keep it runs with --restart unless-stopped , the folder ~/.local/share/bxrig/mail bind-mounted at /data:Z and MP_DATABASE=/data/mailpit.db , so mail survives stop and start. remove deletes the container and the stored mail; --keep-data keeps the folder. start , remove , clear and delete plan first (exit 2 without --yes , --dry-run exits 0); test , open , list , show , env , stop and status act at once. The ports and keep are remembered in mail/meta.json . Container settings: MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY=1 , MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 (an app that logs in works with any user and password, no TLS) and MP_MAX_MESSAGES=5000 , taken from Mailpit's own Docker example. API used (from Mailpit's swagger): GET /api/v1/messages?limit=N ( total , unread , messages[] with ID , From{Name,Address} , To[] , Subject , Created , Size , Attachments as a count, Read , Snippet ), GET /api/v1/message/{ID} ( Text , HTML , Cc , Bcc , Date , Attachments[] with FileName , ContentType , Size ), DELETE /api/v1/messages (all, or a body { "IDs": [...] } ), POST /api/v1/send ( From{Email,Name} , To[{Email}] , Subject , Text ) and GET /view/{ID}.html (opened with xdg-open ). HTTP goes through curl . Without an answer, anything that needs the API exits 4. JSON names differ from the API's on purpose ( mid , sender , sender_address , recipient , subject_line , received , bytes , attachment_count , seen , preview ; for show : to_list , cc_list , bcc_list , sent , body_text , body_html , files[] with file_name , type , bytes ; for test : recipient , subject_line ): MatchBox keeps the capitalisation of the first spelling of a key it sees, so a field called id came out as ID after parsing the API's ID . Fields that do not clash ( total , unread , smtp , web ) keep their names. mail env prints the SMTP settings (host, port, no encryption, no login needed) for a generic list, BoxLang and ColdBox (words only: the exact setting names were not checked), Laravel ( .env ), Spring Boot, Node (nodemailer) and plain environment variables. Control Center page Mail : table of from, received, size, attachment mark and subject; the detail box shows the headers and the wrapped text body of the highlighted message. d plans mail delete ID , c plans mail clear , o runs mail open ID at once, t runs mail test , r reloads. The page reloads itself every 3 seconds (the provider's refreshSeconds() ; ListPage reloads in paint once enough ticks have passed, not while you are typing a filter, and keeps the cursor on the same message by its id ). Providers can also say detailLines() (default 2) to get a taller detail box. Demo data under tui mail --demo . Wizard and menu: one yes or no question mail_catcher (default no) after the databases questions; InitPlan adds the optional step mail-start ( bxrig mail start --yes ), so a missing container engine never stops the plan. Menu: Develop > Mail catcher. # BxRig command contract (A5 draft, v3)

Target (2026-11-09): Hyprland + Noctalia on CachyOS, KDE kept side by side; see plan.md section 19. `setup` is the headline command.

Status: **proposal, no code written.** Note 2026-11-09: the legacy tree in `artifacts/legacy/original/` is the real v0.10.0 source. It is kept as is and never copied, backed up or modified. Decisions here are inputs to M0 hardening (tasks 1.2 to 1.5) and M1 catalog work. Legacy v0.10.0 is a feature reference only (`artifacts/legacy/original/`).

## 1. Grammar

    bxrig <group> <verb> [args...] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] [--quiet]

* Groups mirror the legacy dispatcher so users keep their muscle memory: `setup apps app-manager catalog profile base extras dev web podman ai vector db db-center vm network cloud cloud-center cloud-services files quicklook dictation integrations desktop desktop-keys mac-keys omarchy-base layout themes icons runner menu shortcuts system config first-run doctor setup`.
* Global verbs on every group: `plan` (read-only), `status` (read-only), `doctor` (read-only checks), `help`.
* Mutating verbs: `install`, `apply`, `remove`, `restore`, `enable`, `disable`. All require `--yes`.
* Existing flat commands (`install`, `optional-install`, `profile-install`, `package-status`, `package-source`, ...) stay as aliases until the grouped form ships, then print a deprecation note.
* Unknown flags, duplicate flags, empty arguments and extra positionals are usage errors (exit 2). Nothing runs.
* Note from M0 history: BoxLang `CLIGetArgs()` puts flags in `args.options`, not `args.positionals`. The parser is one shared function, tested once.

## 2. Mutation rules (apply to every mutating verb)

1. No `--yes`: print the exact plan, change nothing, exit 2.
2. `--dry-run` with `--yes`: print the exact plan, change nothing, exit 0.
3. Preflight everything before the first mutation. A preflight failure means zero changes.
4. Never escalate privilege silently. `sudo` is only called for pacman steps shown in the plan.
5. Never run AUR builds as root (exit 4).
6. Every config file touched goes through the config service (backup, atomic replace, journal). No direct writes.
7. Output lists succeeded and failed items separately. No rollback is promised across pacman and yay.
8. External installer scripts (bvm, mvm, `toolchain node`'s nvm, catalog `source: script`) are downloaded to a temp file, their url and sha256 are printed, and they run as the normal user (never root) with no confirmation gate and no flag: the typed `EXECUTE` and `--allow-external-scripts` were removed on 2026-11-10 (owner: running them is the point of the command). Decision 2026-11-09: no checksum pinning for these scripts.
9. Subprocesses are launched with argument arrays, never through a shell string.

## 3. Exit codes

| Code |               Meaning               |                                Example                                 |
|------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Success or no-op                    | already installed, or `--dry-run`                                      |
| 1    | Check negative                      | `package-status` says missing                                          |
| 2    | Usage error or missing confirmation | no `--yes`, unknown flag                                               |
| 3    | Timeout, or item unavailable        | pacman lookup timed out, package not in any repo                       |
| 4    | Precondition failed                 | root with AUR, not Arch, Java missing, not KDE where required          |
| 5    | Official (pacman) phase failed      |                                                                        |
| 6    | AUR (yay) phase failed              |                                                                        |
| 7    | Partial success                     | some items done, some failed; `--json` lists both                      |
| 8    | Config conflict                     | drift detected, symlink or special file at target, concurrent run lock |
| 9    | Internal error                      | bug, unexpected exception                                              |

Codes 0 to 6 match what the native CLI returns today (2, 3, 4, 5, 6 are already used). 1 is already used for check-negative. 7 to 9 are new. Codes are frozen once published and covered by a contract snapshot test.

## 4. `--json`

One JSON object on stdout, nothing else on stdout. Human text goes to stderr.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "command": "profile install",
  "version": "0.11.0-dev",
  "ok": false,
  "exit": 7,
  "dry_run": false,
  "plan":    [{"id": "jq", "source": "pacman", "action": "install"}],
  "done":    [{"id": "jq", "source": "pacman"}],
  "failed":  [{"id": "x", "source": "aur", "reason": "yay exited 1"}],
  "skipped": [{"id": "git", "reason": "already installed"}],
  "warnings": []
}
```

Read-only commands use the same envelope with a `data` field.

## 5. Catalog (single source of truth)

Decision already made: import legacy `catalog/apps.json` (482 entries) as canonical, keeping its 61 default flags. It replaces the hardcoded lists in `src/bxrig.bxs` and `scripts/package-manager.sh`.

Entry schema (legacy fields kept, new fields marked):

|                                  Field                                  |                                                                                                                                             Notes                                                                                                                                             |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `id`, `name`, `kind` (`desktop` `tui` `web`), `category`, `description` | as legacy                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `source` (`pacman` `aur` `pkgbuild` `script` `manual` `web`), `target`  | package name, or URL for web and script                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `pkgbuild` source: `repo`, `path`, `ref`                                | Build with `makepkg` as the normal user from a PKGBUILD in a public git repo, pinned to a full 40-character commit (`catalog check` rejects anything else), then install the result with pacman. Used for Omarchy 4.5 apps (`omacom/omarchy-pkgs`). The PKGBUILD is shown before it is built. |
| `check` (for `script`)                                                  | argv array that exits 0 when installed, for example `["command","-v","pi"]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `default`                                                               | base tier flag                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `source_status`, `source_confirmed`                                     | legacy provenance flags, kept                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `profiles` (new)                                                        | list of profile ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `deps` (new)                                                            | other catalog ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `check` (new)                                                           | optional post-install check, argv array                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `verified_on` (new)                                                     | date the target was confirmed against real repos                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Findings from the legacy data (decisions recorded 2026-11-09):

* **Unverified sources.** 176 entries are `source: manual` (95 tui, 81 desktop). Their package names are unverified. Proposal: a CI job that checks every `pacman`/`aur` target against real repos (Arch container, AUR RPC) and fails on unknown names. `manual` entries stay installable only by explicit user action.
* **Default list mismatch.** 61 flagged default (29 pacman, 18 aur, 14 web). `app-profile.json` `base` lists 46. 20 defaults are not in that base list (for example `ark dolphin dolphin-plugins kio-extras rclone fuse3 sshfs nfs-utils cifs-utils podman-desktop tabby beekeeper-studio google-docs google-sheets google-slides kompare filelight ffmpegthumbs kdegraphics-thumbnailers kimageformats`). 5 base entries are not flagged default (`dbeaver filezilla krdc podman-tui rustdesk`). The 61 flags win. The 5 dropped base entries are `dbeaver` (pacman), `filezilla` (pacman), `krdc` (pacman), `rustdesk` (aur) and `podman-tui` (manual). Pending: keep them as curated (not default), or re-flag any as default.
* **Browsers.** `brave` is `aur` (`brave-bin`) and default. A fresh default install therefore needs yay on day one. Decision: bootstrap installs yay only if it is not already present.
* **Preserve list.** Legacy `preserve` (CachyOS, KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Noctalia, existing user configs) becomes enforced rules, not just text.

Named profiles keep the existing four (`core jvm containers terminal`) and are expressed as catalog `profiles` tags. Later profiles (`web backend ai ops desktop full`) are added only after package names are verified.

Ship vs embed (pending confirmation): the default catalog is embedded in the binary at build time, so there is one file to ship and it always matches the code. An optional `~/.config/bxrig/catalog.json` adds entries or sets `default`/`profiles` on existing ids. It is validated against the same schema and can never delete or replace an embedded entry's `target`, so a bad override cannot redirect an install.

## 6. State and config layout

    ~/.config/bxrig/            same root as legacy
      bxrig.json                global settings
      catalog.json                optional user additions (merge-only)
      ai.json menu.json shortcuts.json ...   one file per feature, as legacy
    ~/.local/state/bxrig/
      journal/                    one record per apply: files, hashes, backup paths
      backups/                    backups, indexed by the journal
      lock                        single-writer lock

`config list|diff|apply|restore` work from the journal, so restore needs only an id. Retention default: keep the last 20 per file. Open: this applies to the user's config files that BxRig writes, not to the legacy source tree.

## 7. Test contract

* A snapshot test freezes `bxrig help`, the exit-code table and the `--json` schema.
* Every mutating verb needs these cases: success, no-op, invalid input, dependency failure, privilege rejection, partial failure, recovery.
* Real-system cases run in `tests/arch/` (non-root, real pacman). Cases needing KDE, Wayland or hardware are marked `manual` and tracked in the acceptance log.

## 8. Catalog check, validation and reporting

`bxrig catalog check [--json] [--online]` plus a CI job that runs it in the Arch container.

**Offline validation (always, no network):** schema version; unique ids; enums for `kind`/`source`; `web` targets are https with no credentials or control characters; package targets match `^[a-zA-Z0-9@._+-]+$`; `default` entries have a non-`manual` source; `profiles` and `deps` reference existing ids; no dependency cycles.

**Online verification (`--online`, CI):** every `pacman` target must resolve with `pacman -Si` (or `-Sg` for groups); every `aur` target must resolve through the AUR RPC (`/rpc/v5/info`); `manual` targets are probed against both and reported as promotable. Results are stored per entry as `verified_on` and a status: `ok`, `moved` (listed source is wrong but another source has it), `missing`, `unverified`.

**Reporting:** a table by status and source for the console, `--json` for tools, and a markdown report in the CI step summary and artifact. Policy: `missing` entries with `default: true` fail CI; `missing` non-default entries are warnings listed in the report; `moved` entries are warnings with the suggested fix.

**First measurement (2026-11-09, stock Arch core/extra only, so CachyOS repos and multilib are not covered):**

|         Check          |                                                                                                                                               Result                                                                                                                                                |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `pacman` targets (118) | 111 resolve, 7 do not: 5 exist in AUR (`git-cola insomnia localsend ulauncher wlogout`), 2 found nowhere (`intellij-idea-community-edition`, `swww`)                                                                                                                                                |
| `aur` targets (64)     | 40 resolve in AUR, 11 are now official (`doggo impala nwg-dock-hyprland opencode podman-desktop rio spotify-launcher superfile television warehouse zenmap`), 13 found nowhere (`beeper ctop dbgate espanso grokbot herder inshellisense notion-desktop pi-agent tmog todoist upnote zap-whatsapp`) |
| `manual` targets (176) | 93 are official packages today (promotable, for example `jq ripgrep-all tmux kitty starship terraform kubectl`), 83 are not                                                                                                                                                                         |

The check must also run against the CachyOS repos on a real CachyOS machine before any `missing` entry is removed.

## 9. Open questions

1. The 5 dropped base entries: keep as curated, or re-flag any as default?
2. Catalog embed with merge-only user override: confirmed?
3. Hyprland features (layout, runner, shortcuts, menus) are now in scope, not deferred.

## 10. Implemented so far (2026-11-09)

* `config list|diff|apply|restore|history` (section 6 design; lock is a file created with `fileWriteExclusive`, temp files and journal records are created exclusive with their mode).
* Global flag check and the `--json` envelope (sections 1 and 4) for the read-only commands.
* `catalog list|show|groups|check|version`: the catalog is schema 3 (`catalog/README.md`) and is embedded in the binary by `bootstrap/gen-catalog.sh` (CI fails if `src/bxrig.bxs` is stale). Filters use the `--name=value` form (`--tier=default --group=infra`), because MatchBox `CLIGetArgs` takes `--name value` as a flag plus a positional. `catalog check` is offline: errors exit 1, warnings (unpinned `pkgbuild` refs, default entries without a package) do not. The user override file is deliberately last (extensibility phase).

## 11. Package commands on the catalog (B2, decided 2026-11-09)

Applies to `plan`, `install-plan`, `install`, `optional-*`, `profile-*`, `package-status`, `package-source`. All read the embedded catalog (schema 3). Hardcoded lists in `Main.bx` go away.

### Selection

    bxrig install                       # tier default
    bxrig install ID [ID...]            # exactly these apps
    bxrig install --profile=NAME        # a profile
    bxrig install --optional            # default tier plus optional tier

* Naming an app is enough. There is **no `--aur` flag** : anything in the catalog installs from its `source` (`pacman`, `aur`, `pkgbuild`, `web`).
* Unknown id: usage error (exit 2), nothing runs.
* Skip reasons: `optional` (not selected), `wrong_shell` and `unresolved` (catalog has no installable source yet; a named `unresolved` app is reported `failed`, exit 3).
* Already installed apps are `skipped` with reason `installed`.
* Section 2 still applies: no `--yes` prints the plan and exits 2; `--dry-run --yes` prints it and exits 0. AUR and `pkgbuild` builds never run as root (exit 4).
* Profiles live in the catalog (0.3.0): a top-level `profiles` list and, per app, a map profile id to `default`/`optional`. `--profile=NAME` installs the profile's `default` members; `--optional` adds its `optional` ones. See `catalog/README.md`.
* Shells: an app may carry `shells` (`hyprland`, `plasma`). The running shell comes from `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, overridable with `--shell=hyprland|plasma|all`. Non-matching apps are `skipped: wrong_shell`; a named app still installs.

### Per-source steps

|   source   |                                                                                                                step                                                                                                                |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `pacman`   | one `pacman -S --needed` call for all pacman apps (sudo shown in the plan)                                                                                                                                                         |
| `aur`      | AUR helper (yay) as the normal user, apps one at a time                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `pkgbuild` | PKGBUILD shown, `makepkg` as the normal user, result installed with pacman                                                                                                                                                         |
| `web`      | a `.desktop` launcher in `~/.local/share/applications/bxrig-<id>.desktop` running `brave --app=URL` (written atomically, no package). The resolver adds `brave` to the plan when a web app is selected and brave is not installed. |

### Result shape (`--json`, inside the section 4 envelope)

`data` for `plan`, `install-plan` and `install`:

```json
{
  "selection": { "mode": "default|ids|profile|optional", "ids": [], "profile": null },
  "would_install": [ { "id": "git", "source": "pacman", "targets": ["git"] } ],
  "done":    [ { "id": "git", "source": "pacman" } ],
  "failed":  [ { "id": "docker", "source": "pacman", "error": "target not found" } ],
  "skipped": [ { "id": "jq", "reason": "optional" } ]
}
```

* `plan` and `--dry-run` fill `would_install` and leave `done`/`failed` empty. A real run fills `done`/`failed` and leaves `would_install` empty.
* Exit: 0 all done or nothing to do; 5 pacman phase failed, 6 AUR/pkgbuild phase failed (only when nothing succeeded); 7 some done and some failed.
* `package-status ID` exits 0 when installed, 1 when missing; `data` is `{ "id", "source", "installed": true|false }`.
* `package-source ID` prints `{ "id", "source", "targets", "tier", "group" }`.

Human output is the same lists, one app per line with its source.

### Open questions

1. Decided: a `web` app counts as installed when its launcher file exists.

## 12. Implemented so far, B2 (2026-11-09)

* Catalog 0.3.0: `profiles`, per-profile tier, `shells` (section 11, `catalog/README.md`).

### 13.1 Commands

    bxrig setup terminal [--default=ghostty] [--also=kitty,foot,...]       install terminals, starter configs with the Nerd Font
    bxrig setup shell [--shell=zsh|fish|bash]                              Starship + shell init, login shell (zsh default)
    bxrig setup xremap [--build=hypr|kde] [--yes]        Cmd-style keys: AUR package, input access, user service
    bxrig setup undo hyprland|plasma|xremap [--yes]      remove only what setup added
    bxrig setup status [--json]
    bxrig tiling on|off|status                           HyprKwin inside Plasma, no logout
    bxrig keys show | render xremap|hyprland|plasma | check | apply [--yes] [--dry-run] [--force]
    bxrig assets list | install [--yes] [--dry-run]

    bxrig runner list | show | doctor | launch | select JSON | set P | menu-set P | launcher-command P JSON | menu-command P JSON   the launcher abstraction (13.9)

* Every target runs, re-runs and undoes on its own; a re-run changes nothing when everything is in place. No `--yes` prints the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` exits 0. Results as `install`: `done` / `failed` / `skipped`, exits 0, 2, 4 (precondition: root, wrong OS or CPU, no sudo, no Plasma, unsupported Plasma, X11, nothing to undo, session not installed), 5 (the pacman step failed), 6 (another step failed with nothing done), 7 (a step failed after earlier ones were done; later steps are skipped), 8 (config drift or lock). Never run as root: sudo is used only for the steps shown in the plan. `--json` is always one envelope on stdout (the config service has a quiet mode for that).

### 13.2 `setup plasma` (HyprKwin)

HyprKwin (`DGBooth/HyprKwin`) is a KWin script with Hyprland-style layouts and keys. It needs Plasma 6.6 or 6.8 on Wayland (6.7 warns, older or X11 exit 4). It is fetched **pinned to a full commit** (v1.2.0, `31abb63`, same rule as PKGBUILDs) into a temp directory and installed with its own `tools/install.sh` as the normal user, which backs up every global shortcut first. Plasma's keys stay Plasma's unless `--keys` (runs `tools/hyprkwin-shortcuts.py apply`; `--undo-keys` restores). The animations effect needs one logout. `setup undo plasma` runs HyprKwin's uninstall. `tiling on|off` sets `hyprkwinEnabled` in `kwinrc` `[Plugins]` and asks KWin to reconfigure over D-Bus (`off` also unloads the script).

### 13.3 `setup hyprland`

Preconditions (exit 4): not root, pacman, CachyOS or Arch, x86_64, sudo. Steps, in order:

1. `packages`: the missing ones of 18 official packages in one `sudo pacman -S --needed` call: `hyprland`, native `noctalia`, `uwsm`, `hyprlock`, `hypridle`, `xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland`, `hyprpolkitagent`, `qt6ct`, `nwg-look`, `hyprpicker`, `grim`, `slurp`, `wl-clipboard`, `brightnessctl`, `kitty`, `adw-gtk-theme`, `noto-fonts`, `noto-fonts-emoji`. Individual packages, never the CachyOS meta-package `cachyos-hypr-noctalia` (it conflicts with `cachyos-desktop-settings`, which the KDE session may rely on). Noctalia is the native `noctalia` package; `noctalia-shell` + `noctalia-qs` are a different Quickshell-based variant that conflicts with `quickshell` (a warning, not an error, if installed). The packages added are remembered (`$XDG_STATE/bxrig/setup-hyprland.json`, mode 600) so `setup undo hyprland` runs `sudo pacman -Rs` on exactly those.
2. `images`: the logo and wallpapers (13.6), missing ones only.
3. `starter`: the Noctalia config and palette, and a first `hyprland.lua` (13.5).
4. `keys`: the shared shortcut files (13.4).

### 13.4 Shortcuts, `keys` and `setup xremap`

One embedded table (`Shortcuts.bx`) holds the shortcuts and is rendered per target. The same keys work on Hyprland and Plasma \[owner\]:

|                    Part                     |          Hyprland          |                            Plasma                            |
|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Tiling and workspace keys                   | Hyprland's own keys        | HyprKwin (same defaults)                                     |
| Cmd-style keys: Super+C, Super+V, Super+Tab | xremap                     | xremap                                                       |
| Logout to the login screen, Super+Shift+Q   | `hl.bind(... "uwsm stop")` | `kglobalshortcutsrc` `[ksmserver] Log Out` via kwriteconfig6 |

* xremap, one shared YAML: Super+C/V send Ctrl+C/V, and Ctrl+Shift+C/V in terminals (a class list in the table); Super+Tab is a plain Alt+Tab remap \[owner\], answered on Hyprland by Noctalia's window switcher (`noctalia msg window-switcher hold`).

* `setup xremap` installs `xremap-hypr-bin` or `xremap-kde-bin` with `yay` (build from `--build`, else the running desktop), adds the udev rule for `/dev/uinput` and the user to the `input` group (both remembered in `setup-xremap.json`, mode 600), writes the shortcut files and enables the user service; `setup undo xremap` reverses only what it added. It needs one logout.

### 13.9 `runner`: the launcher abstraction (port of the legacy `bxrig-runner`)

**Design (owner, 2026-11-10): BxRig is built on an abstraction so runners can be switched.** The rest of BxRig asks for two things and never names a launcher:

    Runner.launch()                      open or toggle the launcher
    Runner.select( prompt, entries )     show [ { label, icon } ] in a menu, return the chosen position (0 = cancelled)

**Super+Space (Hyprland)** is bound once, in the managed `bxrig.lua`, to `bxrig runner launch` (falling back to `noctalia msg panel-toggle launcher` when the chosen launcher cannot run), so `runner set` changes what Super+Space opens without ever editing a keybinding. Which launcher answers is a setting, recorded in `~/.config/bxrig/runner.json` (written atomically); the launcher and the menu provider are chosen separately. **The runner never changes a keybinding or a desktop file** (`doctor` ends with `Shortcut ownership: unchanged`). `set` and `menu-set` are user settings that act at once (no `--yes`), like `tiling`.

Providers are data in `RunnerProviders` (one descriptor each: `id`, `title`, `package`, `launch` argv, and `menu`: dmenu argv with `{prompt}`, `icons`, `returns`). Adding a launcher is adding one descriptor.

|             Provider             |                Launch                |             Menu (dmenu mode)             | Icons | Choice comes back as |       Package       |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------|----------------------|---------------------|
| `noctalia` (default on Hyprland) | `noctalia msg panel-toggle launcher` | none                                      |       |                      | with Noctalia       |
| `walker`                         | `walker`                             | `walker --dmenu`                          | no    | label                | Walker              |
| `rofi` (default menu)            | `rofi -show drun`                    | `rofi -dmenu -i -show-icons -format i -p` | yes   | index                | `rofi`              |
| `fuzzel`                         | `fuzzel`                             | `fuzzel --dmenu --index --prompt`         | yes   | index                | `fuzzel`            |
| `wofi`                           | `wofi --show drun`                   | `wofi --dmenu --insensitive --prompt`     | no    | label                | `wofi`              |
| `vicinae`                        | `vicinae toggle`                     | `vicinae dmenu --prompt`                  | no    | label                | `vicinae-bin` (AUR) |
| `krunner`                        | `krunner`                            | none                                      |       |                      | with KDE            |
| `system`                         | none (the desktop owns it)           | none                                      |       |                      |                     |
| `custom`                         | your `custom_command`                | none                                      |       |                      |                     |

`select` writes the labels (one per line, newlines inside a label become spaces) to a temporary file and runs the provider's command with it on stdin through `sh -c 'exec "$@" < "$f"'`. Providers that understand Rofi's extended dmenu protocol (`label` NUL `icon` US `name`) get icons; the others get plain labels. A non-zero exit, an empty answer, an unknown label or an index out of range is a cancel, never a wrong choice.

    bxrig runner list | show | doctor | launch [--json]
    bxrig runner set P | menu-set P
    bxrig runner launcher-command P JSON_ARGV | menu-command P JSON_ARGV     JSON argument arrays, {prompt} allowed
    bxrig runner select JSON_ENTRIES [--prompt=TEXT] [--json]                prints the 0-based index; exit 1 cancelled, 4 menu cannot run

Commands are JSON argument arrays, never shell strings (a string, an empty array or an empty part exits 4). `list` marks the current choice with `*` (`--json` adds each provider's title, package, icon support and answer format). `doctor` shows the commands and whether each executable is on PATH. `launch` starts the launcher detached (exit 4 for `system` or a missing program). The wizard offers Noctalia, Walker, Rofi, Fuzzel and Wofi; Vicinae, KRunner and `custom` work from the command line. `hyprrunner` was dropped (no package found, 2026-11-10). Fuzzel and Wofi flags are from their man pages.

### 13.10 `db`: local databases and search engines as containers (port of the legacy `bxrig-db` and `bxrig-vector`)

    bxrig db engines | list [--json]
    bxrig db start ENGINE [--name N] [--port P] [--password-file FILE | --ask-password] [--yes] [--dry-run]    create, or start a stopped one; never replaces a container
    bxrig db stop|status|logs ENGINE [--name N]
    bxrig db remove ENGINE [--name N] [--keep-data] --yes              removes the container AND its data (volume and password file); --keep-data keeps the data
    bxrig db info ENGINE [--name N] [--show-password]                  where it listens and how to connect (password masked by default)
    bxrig db engine [podman|docker]                                    which engine runs them (podman by default, saved in ~/.config/bxrig/db.json)
    bxrig db menu                                                      the control center, on the runner's menu provider (needs a terminal program)

Exit codes: 0 done, 2 usage or no `--yes` (the plan is printed; `--dry-run` exits 0), 4 precondition (no container engine, unknown or unsupported engine, bad name or port, `vm.max_map_count` too low), 6 the container command failed. `--json` gives the standard envelope.

**Rules.** Services listen on `127.0.0.1` only. A container that exists is never replaced (a stopped one is started; a running one is left alone). Containers are named `bxrig-db-<engine>-<name>` (name defaults to `default`; letters, digits and hyphens) and labelled `io.bxrig.database=true`. Data lives in a **named volume** with the container's name, not a host folder (`db remove` deletes it together with the container and the password files, so the next start is a clean database; `--keep-data` keeps them, and starting the same name again then reuses the volume and its password): rootless containers cannot write to a bind-mounted folder as the image's own user (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch and Meilisearch run as non-root). **Choosing the password:** by default one is generated. `--password-file FILE` uses the first line of a file you made; `--ask-password` asks twice at the terminal without echo (`/dev/tty`, so it needs a terminal; the plan never prompts). A password is **never** a command-line value, so it cannot land in shell history or the process list. It must be 8 to 128 characters with no whitespace (OpenSearch also needs upper and lower case, a digit and a special character). It applies only when the container is created (the image sets it on first start of the data volume): a second start never changes it, an existing container refuses one, and a kept data volume (from `remove --keep-data`) keeps the password it was made with (a different choice is refused). Engines without a password (Redis, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate) and Couchbase (set in its web console) refuse the options. The user name is fixed per engine (`postgres`, `root`, `admin`, `elastic`). Generated passwords (24 random bytes as hex) go in `~/.local/share/bxrig/databases/<container>/` (`password` and `database.env`, mode 600, plus `meta.json` with the port) and reach the container through `--env-file`, never on a command line. Nothing changes system settings: when `vm.max_map_count` is too low `start` stops with the `sudo sysctl -w` line to run. Images are pinned and were checked on Docker Hub on 2026-11-10 (Elasticsearch's from Elastic's docs).

### 13.11 `dotfiles`: your own dotfiles repository (decided with the owner 2026-11-11)

    bxrig dotfiles plan REPO [--method=chezmoi|yadm|stow|links] [--json]    clones the repo into BxRig's data folder; changes nothing in your home
    bxrig dotfiles apply REPO [--method=M] [--overwrite] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
    bxrig dotfiles status | undo [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]

`REPO` is a git URL or a local path. **The method is detected** (`--method` overrides): `chezmoi` (`.chezmoiroot`, `.chezmoiignore`, or `dot_` / `.chezmoi*` names), then `yadm` (`.config/yadm/`, or `##` alternate names), then `stow` (`.stowrc`, `.stow-local-ignore`, or only top-level package folders that hold dotfiles), else `links`.

**Your dotfiles win, but nothing is replaced unasked.** The plan splits the repo's files into new, already in place (a link to the repo, or an identical file) and **conflicts** (files you already have that would be replaced; chezmoi templates always count). `apply --yes` needs your approval of the conflicts: `--overwrite`, or a `y` at the prompt (read from `/dev/tty`, so a headless run without `--overwrite` exits 2 and changes nothing). Every replaced file is first moved into `~/.local/state/bxrig/backups/dotfiles/<time>/`; if a step then fails (exit 6) the originals are put back. `status` shows what was applied; `undo --yes` removes the links BxRig made (`stow -D` for stow) and restores the originals (for chezmoi and yadm only the originals come back: the files those tools created stay, remove them with the tool).

|  Method   |                                            Files go to your home by                                            |                                Applied with                                 |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `links`   | one symlink per file (folders are never replaced by a link)                                                    | `ln -s`                                                                     |
| `stow`    | each top-level folder is a package                                                                             | `stow -d CLONE -t HOME -R PACKAGES`                                         |
| `chezmoi` | `dot_`, `private_`, `executable_`, ... prefixes and `.tmpl` are mapped to the plain path for the conflict list | `chezmoi apply --source CLONE --force`                                      |
| `yadm`    | `##` alternate suffixes are mapped to the plain name                                                           | `yadm clone -f --no-bootstrap REPO` (`yadm pull` when it is already set up) |

Repo-only files (`.git`, `README*`, `LICENSE*`, `.gitignore`, `.stow-local-ignore`...) are never linked. A missing tool (`chezmoi`, `yadm`, `stow`; Arch `extra`) is installed with `sudo pacman -S --needed` as the first step of `apply` (the plan says so). One repository can be set up at a time: a second one is refused (exit 4) until `undo`. Exits: 0 done, 2 no `--yes` or conflicts not approved, 4 precondition (cannot clone, unknown method, nothing to apply, tool not installable), 6 a step failed. The wizard's Import page asks for the repository (empty skips); `init` runs `dotfiles apply REPO` **last**, so your files win over the starter configs, and the conflict question appears at the terminal.

Tested against real git repositories and fake tools (`stow`, `chezmoi`, `yadm`, `pacman`); the real tools have not been run. Private repositories and credentials are git's business (SSH keys or a credential helper must already work).

### 13.12 Apps: Basic or Customize, and your defaults (decided with the owner 2026-11-11)

The wizard's Apps page asks **how you want your apps** : **Basic** (the default: an opinionated, recommended set) or **Customize**.

* **Basic** runs `bxrig install --shell=hyprland|plasma|all` for the desktop(s) you chose: the catalog's **default tier** (64 apps), desktop-specific ones only for their desktop. Nothing is asked.
* **Customize** shows one extra page per catalog group (11, built from the catalog by `AppPages`, after the Apps page): a multi-choice list per category with the default apps ticked, each option showing its description and the macOS equivalent. Only what is ticked is installed (`bxrig install ID...`, one command), minus apps that belong to a desktop you did not choose. Categories the wizard asks about itself are not repeated: AI "Coding orchestration", Desktop "Launchers", Terminal "Terminal" and Development "Shell". Answer keys: `apps_<group>_<category>` (a list of app ids). Web apps are one of the groups, like any other.
* **Default browser** (`default_browser`, asked in both modes, default Brave): installed if needed, then set with `bxrig default browser ID`.
